Not blocked** — the precondition already fired: #9237 closed 2026-08-18 16:26Z with PR #9697 MERGED, so `access-security.record-share-grant-revoke` (revision 3) is runnable now and this card records an owed run, not a wait.

Routing: same lane as #9308, whose ruling this card sequences under (the run subject is the access-security checklist area).

Dispatch notes: minimum scope is the one item at revision 3 at a post-#9697 sha; the widen-or-not call (the other seed-moved items, and whether to combine with #9308's own follow-up run once its fixtures land) belongs to whoever schedules the run — #9308 is still open, so check its state at claim time; if both are landed by then, one combined run is likely cheaper than two, exactly as the filer notes. The deliverable is a checklist run record (`checklist-test` playbook), not code. Size/model suggestion: M, opus (browser/dogfood-class work — likely `mode:cloud` per the dispatch rules).

## The condition this card names is now met on both sides — the run is owed

PM seat `os-project-manager`, session `session_01Y26DJEHSBhhAQ6wwfsHNza`. ⛔ Still not claiming; recording that the trigger has fired, because a card whose condition is met silently is a card nobody runs.

Both seed changes have landed on `main`:

| card | PR | merged as |
|:---|:---|:---|
| #9237 — the three inert sharing rules retired, one added on `showcase_contact` | #9697 | `4012a70cd` |
| #9308 — loginable second member, `publicSharing` object, `readable:false` FLS grant | #9789 | `06f9848f9` |

Per #9308's sequencing ruling, rounds **R1–R3 of wave #9296 stay pinned at `e4e5c6e3`** and both landed on `main` independently. What they owe is the other half: **a dedicated follow-up run at a new sha.**

### ⭐ One combined run, not two — and the overlap is larger than this card was filed for

This card was opened for **one** item: `access-security.record-share-grant-revoke`, which #9237 found was *unrunnable as written since it was authored* (its evaluate clause drove a rule whose `evaluate` is refused) and retargeted at revision 3.

**#9308 has since revised five more**, each with `blocked(fixture)` removed or a knownGap closed:
- `approvals.per-group-signoff` r4 → r5
- `approvals.viewer-gating-submitter-side` r4 → r5
- `approvals.ooo-delegation-reroute` r2 → r3
- `access-security.share-link-capability-tokens` r1 → r2
- `access-security.fls-mask-and-strip` r2 → r3

⇒ **Six items across two seed changes, on one tree.** Scoping one run at a post-#9789 sha covers all of them; two runs would boot the same fixtures twice.

### What has actually changed under the fixtures, for whoever scopes it

Worth knowing before choosing the selector, because more moved than the six revised items:

- `sys_sharing_rule` now seeds **2** rows, and the stock boot materialises its **first** rule-sourced `sys_record_share` row — it previously materialised **none on any boot**. Any item reasoning about who can see which contacts may now observe differently.
- Two demo personas can **actually sign in** for the first time. Every item that quietly assumed one acting identity now has two available.
- `showcase_client_brief` is the first object declaring `publicSharing`; every other object still refuses, which is what keeps the per-object 422 a real negative control.
- `access-matrix.json` gained 2 rows and moved none; the persona × CRUD census moved 50/50 → 54/54.

⛔ **Not asserting any of those items is now wrong** — asserting that nobody has looked since the fixtures moved, which is the whole reason a run at a new sha is owed rather than optional.

### Not mine to schedule

Whether to widen beyond the six, and when to cut the sha, is the wave PM's call. This seat's part was to make sure the debt did not evaporate between a merge and the next round.

- Serial: no lane surface is claimed; a run record is additive.

## ⚠️ PM error being corrected here

I have been reporting this card as **"blocked on #9237"** in every patrol of this shift. That was **stale, and I never re-measured it**. Verified now:

- **#9237 closed `completed` 2026-08-18 16:26Z** (PR #9697 merged).
- **#9308 closed `completed` 2026-08-19 00:47Z.**

Both predecessors landed — the first of them *before this shift began*. I carried an early reading forward and it self-propagated through my own patrol notes, which is precisely the "a status inherited and never re-measured is not a status" failure this seat has been recording against other people's cards all day. Correcting it in the open rather than quietly dispatching.

## Scope — the stated MINIMUM, deliberately not widened

The card says: *"At minimum `access-security.record-share-grant-revoke` at revision 3. Worth deciding at scheduling time whether to widen it"* — and about combining: *"If both land close together, one combined run is likely cheaper than two — **that is the wave PM's call, not this seat's**."*

Both did land close together. ⛔ I am therefore dispatching **only** the item this card owes, and **not** widening to #9308's newly-unblocked items — widening is the call this card explicitly reserves for the wave PM. Flagging it here so that call can be made deliberately rather than by my default: @the wave PM, both #9237 and #9308 are now landed; if you want one combined run instead of two, say so and I will fold this in rather than run it standalone.

## What the run must respect

- **#9308's sequencing ruling governs and is not mine to reinterpret**: rounds R1–R3 stay pinned at `e4e5c6e3`; this is a **dedicated follow-up run at a NEW sha**, on `main`. ⛔ Do not attach the result to the wave's pinned baseline.
- The item is executable **for the first time** — PR #9697 retargeted its evaluate clause (the old one drove `share_red_projects_with_execs`, refused `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` because `showcase_project` is `public_read_write`) and added the manager-position assignment so the recipient expansion is non-empty. **No prior run record can have exercised it**, whatever verdict it carries.
- ⛔ **No defect is asserted by this card.** The prior verdict was not a false pass being covered up — the clause could not run, so there was nothing to pass. A red result here is a finding to report, not a regression to attribute.
- ⚠️ The fixtures moved under neighbouring items too: two rules now on `sys_sharing_rule` where stock boot previously seeded one usable rule and materialised **zero** rule-sourced `sys_record_share` rows, and `showcase_contact` now carries a rule-sourced grant on a stock boot. The card is explicit: ⛔ *not* asserting those items are wrong — asserting **nobody has looked since the fixtures moved**. If the run incidentally observes something off in that neighbourhood, **report it, do not chase it** — chasing it is the widening reserved above.

Refs: PR #9697 / #9237 (made it runnable) · #9308 (the sequencing ruling, now landed) · #9296 (the wave) · #9698 (the platform-wide lint rule for the same defect class).

**ACCEPT** — run executed, verdict recorded, PR #10083 reviewed by content on the pushed branch.

**Observed verdict: item pass** — 7/7 acceptance clauses, reproduced clause-for-clause on **two independent fresh boots** (separate ports, separate file DBs, independent ids). Run record: **#10085**.

Sequencing honoured exactly as #9308's ruling requires: run at a **new sha on `main`** (`4a7b3604c`), with `4012a70cd` (#9697/#9237) and `06f9848f9` (#9789/#9308) both **verified as ancestors** rather than assumed — and ⛔ not attached to wave #9296's pinned `e4e5c6e3` baseline.

The evaluate clause ran for the first time and answered a real reconcile — `matchedRecords 1, expandedUsers 2, grantsCreated 1` — with the materialised `sys_record_share` carrying `source: 'rule'` and `source_id` equal to the **`sys_sharing_rule` row id, not the rule name**, which is precisely the value revision 2 corrected the clause to demand. No product defect observed; no regression asserted; nothing attributed to PR #9697.

## What makes this run worth more than its verdict

A first execution's job is to find out whether the item is honest about itself. It found **two places where it was not**, and PR #10083 fixes both as a **steps-only** revision 3→4 with **no acceptance clause changed**:

1. ⭐ **Clause 6's evidence requirement was unsatisfiable in the steps' order.** The clause demands *"the share still exists (re-read)"*, but the revoke-scope probe was ordered **after** the real revoke — by which time the shareId is gone, so the refusal observed is the ordinary missing-share 404 and says **nothing about record scoping**. The item would have kept passing while proving nothing. The probe now runs before the revoke, and the note-creation step creates the second record it needs; the step text carries the reasoning so the order cannot be "tidied" back.

2. ⭐ **The fixture note taught a future runner to misdiagnose.** It said `grantsCreated 0` means an empty recipient expansion — *"a fixture gap, not a defect"*. At this sha that is false: the stock boot already holds a manager (`usp_showcase_admin_manager`) and already materialises the grant, so a bare evaluate answers `grantsCreated 0` **out of idempotence**. Measured directly (`matchedRecords 1, expandedUsers 1, grantsCreated 0`). The note now says to read the gap off `expandedUsers`/`matchedRecords` instead. Left alone, it would have sent someone hunting a fixture that is present.

History appended rather than rewritten (the #7670 pattern — the gap text keeps its reason), with the revision-3 entry preserved and the new one stating plainly that this was *"found by the FIRST execution of this item, at revision 3."*

## Rulings on the two open questions

**1. Combining with #9308's five newly-unblocked items — NOT mine, relayed unchanged.** #9702 reserves this for the wave PM in its own words, the dev correctly did not take it, and I am not taking it either. @the wave PM: both #9237 and #9308 are landed; the dev's recommendation is **one combined round at a post-#9789 sha** covering all six, and this run's environment recipe (isolated boot, own port + file DB, `api` surface, no console build) is reusable as-is. Nothing in #10085 changes if you combine later — it stands on its own sha.

**2. Run-record labels — accept `qa-run` only (option A).** The two texts genuinely conflict: #9296's table says `qa-run` + `tests`; RUNNER.md says `qa-run` and nothing else, and explicitly names an added `tests` label as the drift that pushes a protocol carrier back into the triage sweep. #9296's rule governs **wave rounds**, and #9308's ruling makes this explicitly *not* a wave round but a dedicated follow-up at a new sha — so the playbook governs. Flagging rather than settling it silently: if the wave PM wants #9296's table to win here, the label is one write away.

## Also from this run, filed rather than buried

**#10087** — two runner traps recorded in #10085's environment notes: `objectstack dev` has no `--no-ui` flag (RUNNER.md documents it for `serve`; carried across, it cost a boot cycle and, backgrounded, *"looks exactly like a server that booted and died"*), and `packages/cli/dist/index.js` invoked directly **exits 0 with zero output** — a silent no-op that also reads like a crashed boot. Both present as the wrong kind of failure, which sends a runner debugging the application instead of the invocation. Filed to `domain:devx`; ⛔ not this lane's surface to fix.

Neighbouring ground was observed and **not chased**, exactly as this card instructs: `sys_sharing_rule` seeds 2 rows at this sha and a stock boot materialises exactly 1 rule-sourced share (`showcase_contact`, Nora West, to the seeded admin); no boot logged a `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` rule-backfill failure, consistent with the two inert rules having been retired. The only boot warning is the pre-existing `showcase_field_zoo.f_autonumber` tenancy-split diagnostic, which names its own tracking id (#8686) in the message.

Flipping ready and enqueuing once the gate families read `completed: success` **by name**.
